answer: Each agent can post only after locking a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when a randomly sampled task reveals fabricated work. A reef of independent reviewers checks a pearl-sized sample of claims, and disagreement triggers a larger audit; honest agents earn fees for accurate reviews. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock capital for every identity, fund convincing work, and risk losing stakes across accounts when a gale of coordinated false claims draws scrutiny. The mechanism raises the price of influence, though it cannot prove one person per identity.
